007901:     // The read-modify-write runs in the unit the field is accessed through,
007902:     // which is the declared type unless packing narrowed it; the value
007903:     // truncates into that unit first, and the mask keeps only the field's own
007904:     // bits either way. A span no integer is the width of takes one
007905:     // read-modify-write per piece instead.
007906:     // A `_Bool` bit-field reaches the read-modify-write like any other, through

007973: // Whether a promoted-member search has already queued `type`.
007974: //
007975: // The two searches below (this one and c_ir_promoted_member_path) walk the
007976: // anonymous nested aggregates of one struct or union, so their work lists hold
007977: // a handful of entries and almost always exactly one. Both used to answer this
007978: // question with a `bool` array indexed by type id, allocated and memset per
007979: // call over the whole program type table: 72.167 calls at a mean capacity of
007980: // 17.432 types, 1,26 GB of zeroing per self-host compile, 6,74% of every
007981: // stage-1 L1d miss for a set that never held more than a few members (audit
007982: // 2026-08-22T084855Z). The work list is the visited set; scanning it costs
007983: // less than clearing the table did.
007984: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_type_queued(const IrTypeId* queued, u32 count, IrTypeId type)
007985: {
007986:     bool found = false;
007987:     for (u32 index = 0; index < count; index += 1)
007988:     {
007989:         if (queued[index].value == type.value)
007990:         {
007991:             found = true;
007992:             break;
007993:         }
007994:     }
007995:     return found;
007996: }

007998: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_recover_place_from_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value);
007999: 
008000: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_field_place_from_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, CToken access, CToken member)
008001: {
008002:     if (operand.value >= builder->function->value_count)
008003:     {
008004:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
008005:     }
008006:     if (c_token_is_punctuator(&access, C_PUNCTUATOR_ARROW) && c_ir_value_contains_label_provenance(builder, operand))
008007:     {
008008:         builder->failure_message = S8("a label-provenance value may not be used as an addressable place");
008009:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
008010:     }
008011:     IrValueId base = operand;
008012:     IrTypeId aggregate_type_id = builder->function->values[operand.value].canonical_type;
008013:     if (c_token_is_punctuator(&access, C_PUNCTUATOR_ARROW))
008014:     {
008015:         operand = c_ir_decay_array_value_if_needed(builder, operand, c_ir_token_source_range(builder, access));
008016:         if (operand.value >= builder->function->value_count)
008017:         {
008018:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
008019:         }
008020:         aggregate_type_id = builder->function->values[operand.value].canonical_type;
008021:         IrType* pointer_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, aggregate_type_id);
008022:         if (!pointer_type || pointer_type->kind != IR_TYPE_POINTER)
008023:         {
008024:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
008025:         }
008026:         aggregate_type_id = pointer_type->element_type;
008027:         base = ir_function_add_value(builder->arena, builder->function,
008028:                                      (IrValue){
008029:                                          .canonical_type = aggregate_type_id,
008030:                                          .definition = IR_INSTRUCTION_ID_INVALID,
008031:                                          .category = IR_VALUE_PLACE,
008032:                                          .is_read_only = builder->function->values[operand.value].points_to_read_only,
008033:                                          .is_volatile = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, aggregate_type_id)->is_volatile,
008034:                                      });
008035:         IrSourceRange dereference_source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, access);
008036:         IrInstruction dereference = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_DEREFERENCE, aggregate_type_id);
008037:         dereference.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
008038:         dereference.operands[0] = operand;
008039:         dereference.operand_count = 1;
008040:         dereference.result = base;
008041:         IrInstructionId dereference_id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, dereference, dereference_source);
008042:         builder->function->values[base.value].definition = dereference_id;
008043:     }
008044:     else if (!c_token_is_punctuator(&access, C_PUNCTUATOR_DOT))
008045:     {
008046:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
008047:     }
008048:     else if (builder->function->values[operand.value].category != IR_VALUE_PLACE)
008049:     {
008050:         IrInstructionId definition = builder->function->values[operand.value].definition;
008051:         if (definition.value >= builder->function->instruction_count)
008052:         {
008053:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
008054:         }
008055:         IrInstruction* instruction = &builder->function->instructions[definition.value];
008056:         if (instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_LOAD && instruction->operand_count == 1)
008057:         {
008058:             // The load only materialized the aggregate for the expression
008059:             // walk; `E.m` designates a member of the object E names and never
008060:             // reads the whole of it. Drop it when it is still the last
008061:             // instruction emitted, the way the address-of arm of
008062:             // c_ir_apply_operation drops the load behind `&E`. The token peek
008063:             // in the member arm keeps the place before the load exists, but it
008064:             // only sees the token that follows the member identifier, so a
008065:             // group between the two accesses hides the `.` from it:
008066:             // `(*o).in.x` and `&(((T *)0)->in).v[3]` arrive here with the copy
